mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate above 3% over a three-month window signals a tightening cycle that raises discount rates and reduces present value of future corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) in periods when FEDFUNDS exceeds 3% for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% coincides with reduced corporate revenue expectations, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: No statistically significant negative correlation (p > 0.05) between GDPC1 YoY declines > 2% and S&P 500 60-day forward returns.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the unemployment rate above 6% for two consecutive months signals deteriorating consumer and business confidence, which depresses earnings growth and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly lower (p > 0.10) when UNRATE exceeds 6% for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) below its 12-month moving average for four consecutive months indicates supply-side stress, which raises input costs and reduces profit margins, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: No significant negative relationship (p > 0.05) between INDPRO contraction and S&P 500 20-day forward returns.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both the federal funds rate and the Consumer Price Index above their respective 12-month moving averages signals a dual monetary and inflationary shock that erodes real purchasing power and depresses equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.05) when both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL exceed their 12-month moving averages simultaneously.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the Housing Starts index (HOUST) above its 12-month moving average for six consecutive months signals robust residential demand, which correlates with higher corporate earnings in construction and related sectors, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: No significant positive correlation (p > 0.05) between sustained HOUST strength and S&P 500 20-day forward returns.

mechanism_narrative: A coordinated rise in both payroll employment (PAYEMS) and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) over a two-month period indicates a paradoxical labor market signal where headline employment growth coexists with deteriorating labor market quality, which can foreshadow negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days due to uncertainty and productivity concerns.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS > 12M MA AND UNRATE > 6.0% in same month for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly lower (p > 0.10) during episodes where PAYEMS exceed their 12-month moving average while UNRATE is above 6% for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent decline in Real Personal Savings (RSAFS) below its 12-month moving average for eight consecutive months signals reduced household buffer capacity, which increases sensitivity to economic shocks and tends to precede negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: No significant negative correlation (p > 0.05) between prolonged RSAFS weakness and S&P 500 60-day forward returns.
